title: Angry Thomas Tuchel made ferocious demand to England star before Norway goal | talkSPORT
text:
The Three Lions manager appeared a frustrated figure on the touchline as his side failed to have a single shot before the first hydration break.

He raged at his team during the break, picking out Elliot Anderson and Madueke in particular to speak to in the dugout.

Speaking from inside the Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, talkSPORT's England correspondent, Faye Carruthers, said: "The first person Tuchel went over to was Anderson.

"A few times he wanted him to be a little bit closer over to the left-hand side. It's been really interesting watching him. He's been so frustrated with the lack of energy.

"He's now deep in conversation with Noni Madueke, that's what he needs. He's actually quite angry and telling him what he needs him to do down that right-hand side. Because we potentially would have had a lot of joy down there.

"We saw it with Anthony Gordon down the left-hand side, every time Thomas Tuchel told him to hug the touchline on the left-hand side, he went out there.

"It was John Stones with the ball across to him and we had joy. We won a corner. We drove at the defence. There's just not enough speed and that's what he's telling him."

Former England captain Stuart Pearce then added: "He's in Madueke's ear quite ferociously. That's good management on what I'm seeing.

"Because I think our two wide players hold the key in this game because that's probably where they're at the weakest."

"I'm looking at Thomas Tuchel's body language here, he is at full throttle down there with his body language."

Madueke only attempted three dribbles in the first half, giving away one foul and sending a cross straight out for a goal kick.

The Arsenal winger lost possession five times in the first period too, but also almost set up Nico O'Reilly for a tap-in.

England then conceded shortly after the hydration break to go 1-0 down, but Jude Bellingham hit back just before half time.

Harry Kane then chipped in to seemingly give the Three Lions the lead, but the offside flag denied him.

And at the break, Madueke was substituted by Tuchel and replaced by Bukayo Saka, with Declan Rice taken off for Eberechi Eze.

Despite going into half time at 1-1, talkSPORT's Adrian Durham and Pearce were not happy with the performance.

Durham ranted: "Jude Bellingham has saved us yet again. I actually think Thomas Tuchel should get stuck into them at half-time. I actually thought that first half, in the main, up to the goal, was a complete embarrassment from England.

"That first half was everything that Tuchel said it wouldn't be."

He added: "Wow, I mean there's a lot of work for Thomas Tuchel to do, because I just felt we were a shambles.

"And if you look at the hydration break, Thomas Tuchel got stuck into the players and they got worse, they got even worse after the hydration break."

On Madueke specifically, Durham continued: "He's seen a lot of the ball in the first seven minutes, but we saw what Madueke's all about.

"He took on his man once, he went backwards four times, he inexplicably got caught offside another time.

"This guy is getting a massive opportunity at this World Cup, he's being trusted by his manager, Thomas Tuchel, in massive games, a quarter-final of a World Cup.

"And he's up against a full-back he knows he can beat in his sleep, and he passes it backwards all the time. First minute and last minute of the 45, he took his man on, it's just not good enough."

In the second half, things didn't get much better for England, as they continued to struggle to create any chances.

Norway had the best chance, hitting the bar, but the game went to extra time, as neither side could find a winner.

Bellingham would soon step up again though, tapping home a rebound to give the Three Lions a 2-1 lead.

And that was enough to book a place in the World Cup semi-finals, putting England just two wins away from glory.
